subject: chemistry

concepts.title: Average Rate of Reaction
concepts.definition: The speed of a chemical process measured by evaluating the concentration change of a substance over a specified time duration.
concepts.key_idea: Change in reactant or product concentration divided by the total time taken.
question_patterns: calculate the average rate of reaction between time intervals
find the average rate of disappearance of reactant
determine average rate of reaction when concentration changes from c1 to c2
what is the average rate of reaction in mol L-1 s-1
how much is the average rate over a time interval

solution_steps.explain: subtract final concentration c2 from initial concentration c1
divide concentration change by time interval delta_t to obtain average rate

concepts.title: Stoichiometry and Rates of Formation or Disappearance
concepts.definition: The rate of change of individual chemical species related through their respective balancing coefficients in a chemical equation.
concepts.key_idea: Divide species consumption or formation rate by its stoichiometric coefficient to equalize reaction rates.
question_patterns: calculate the rate of formation of product given rate of consumption of reactant
find the rate of production of NO2 from decomposition of N2O5
determine the rate of disappearance of reactant from product appearance rate
what is the rate of formation of species with stoichiometric coefficient
how much product is formed per unit time given reactant consumption rate

solution_steps.explain: multiply reactant rate by product coefficient and divide by reactant coefficient

concepts.title: Overall Order of Reaction
concepts.definition: The total sum of exponents to which reactant concentration terms are raised in an experimental rate law expression.
concepts.key_idea: Overall order equals the sum of individual reaction orders with respect to each reactant.
question_patterns: calculate the overall order of reaction from rate expression
find the order of reaction given rate = k [A]^x [B]^y
determine total order when individual orders are given
what is the overall order for a rate law
how to calculate reaction order from powers of concentration terms

solution_steps.explain: add exponent of reactant A and exponent of reactant B

concepts.title: Effect of Concentration Change on Reaction Rate
concepts.definition: The quantitative factor by which a reaction rate changes when reactant concentrations are scaled according to the reaction order.
concepts.key_idea: Scaling reactant concentration by a factor increases reaction rate by that factor raised to the order.
question_patterns: calculate how reaction rate changes when concentration is doubled
find the change in rate when concentration of reactant is increased n times
determine new rate when concentration of second order reactant is tripled
what is the factor by which rate increases on changing concentration
how much does rate increase when reactant concentration changes

solution_steps.action: raise concentration scale factor to reaction order
solution_steps.explain: compute conc_factor to the power of order

concepts.title: Molecularity of an Elementary Reaction
concepts.definition: The integer count of colliding chemical species that simultaneously interact in a single elementary reaction step.
concepts.key_idea: Molecularity is a theoretical integer property applicable only to single-step elementary steps.
question_patterns: distinguish between order and molecularity of a reaction
what is the molecularity of an elementary reaction
why complex reactions cannot have molecularity greater than three
identify molecularity for unimolecular and bimolecular steps
explain rate determining step in complex mechanism

solution_steps.action: identify reacting species in elementary step
solution_steps.explain: count total number of reactant molecules colliding simultaneously in the rate-determining elementary step
ensure molecularity is a positive integer (1, 2, or 3) and apply only to elementary reactions

concepts.title: Half-Life of Zero Order Reaction
concepts.definition: The time required for half the reactant to react in a zero-order process, which is directly proportional to initial concentration.
concepts.key_idea: Zero order half-life scales directly with initial concentration and inversely with the rate constant.
question_patterns: calculate half-life of a zero order reaction
find rate constant of zero order reaction given half-life
determine time for half completion of zero order reaction
what is the half-life for zero order process
how much time is required to reduce initial concentration by half in zero order

solution_steps.explain: double the value of rate constant k
divide initial concentration by 2k to get half life

concepts.title: Half-Life of First Order Reaction
concepts.definition: The time needed for half of a reactant to decompose in a first-order process, independent of starting concentration.
concepts.key_idea: First order half-life depends purely on the rate constant and is constant throughout the reaction.
question_patterns: calculate half-life of a first order reaction
find rate constant from half-life of first order process
determine half life period given k = 5.5e-14 s-1
what is the half-life of first order decay
how to compute half-life for radioactive disintegration

solution_steps.action: divide ln(2) constant by rate constant
solution_steps.explain: divide 0.693 by rate constant k to obtain half life

concepts.title: Pseudo First Order Reaction
concepts.definition: A higher-order reaction that exhibits first-order kinetics because one reactant is present in huge excess.
concepts.key_idea: Excess species concentration remains practically constant, simplifying the rate law to first order.
question_patterns: explain pseudo first order reaction with example
why hydrolysis of ethyl acetate is pseudo first order
what makes inversion of cane sugar a pseudo first order process
identify pseudo order conditions when water is in large excess
determine order when one reactant concentration is fixed

solution_steps.explain: verify if one reactant concentration is vastly greater than the other so its change is negligible
combine constant excess concentration with rate constant into pseudo first-order rate constant

concepts.title: Temperature Dependence and Temperature Coefficient
concepts.definition: The exponential scaling of reaction rates when temperature increases in ten-degree increments.
concepts.key_idea: Reaction rate approximately doubles for every ten kelvin increase in temperature.
question_patterns: calculate increase in rate of reaction when temperature rises by delta_T
find rate factor when temperature increases by 30 degrees
determine how many times rate increases for temperature rise
what is the effect of 10 K rise in temperature on rate constant
how much does reaction speed up when heated

concepts.title: Role of Catalyst in Chemical Kinetics
concepts.definition: An added substance that speeds up a chemical reaction by providing an alternative pathway with reduced activation energy.
concepts.key_idea: Catalysts lower the activation energy barrier without altering overall reaction enthalpy or equilibrium constant.
question_patterns: explain the effect of catalyst on activation energy
does catalyst change gibbs energy or equilibrium constant
how catalyst speeds up reaction rate
what is intermediate complex theory of catalysis
describe energy profile diagram with and without catalyst

solution_steps.explain: catalyst lowers activation energy barrier providing lower energy intermediate path
confirm that enthalpy change, Gibbs free energy, and equilibrium constant remain unchanged

concepts.title: Collision Theory of Chemical Reactions
concepts.definition: A model asserting that chemical reactions occur when molecules collide with sufficient energy and correct orientation.
concepts.key_idea: Effective collisions require both threshold energy and favorable steric orientation.
question_patterns: explain collision theory of bimolecular reactions
what is steric factor or probability factor P
define collision frequency and effective collisions
what conditions must be met for a collision to produce products
why complex molecules deviate from simple collision theory predictions

solution_steps.explain: colliding species must possess energy equal to or exceeding threshold energy
molecules must be aligned with correct spatial orientation for effective bond breaking and formation
